(21 April 2011) | average attendance = 4,204 | prevseason = [[2009–10 Saudi Professional League|2009–10]] | nextseason = [[2011–12 Saudi Professional League|2011–12]] }} The '''2010–11 Saudi Professional League''' (known as the '''[[Zain Group|Zain]] Professional League''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 35th season of the [[Saudi Pro League]], the top Saudi professional league for [[association football]] clubs, since its establishment in [[1976–77 Saudi Premier League|1976]]. The season began on 14 August 2010, and ended on 20 May 2011.{{cite web |title=Fixtures & Results |url=http://slstat.com/spl2010-2011en/champtable.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160322031155/http://slstat.com/spl2010-2011en/champtable.php |archive-date=22 March 2016 |url-status=dead}} [[Al Hilal SFC|Al-Hilal]] were the [[2009–10 Saudi Pro League|defending champions]].{{cite web |title=الهلال بطلاً للدوري السعودي 2010 |url=http://www.alriyadh.com/492692}} The league was contested by the 12 teams from the [[2009–10 Saudi Pro League|2009–10 season]] as well as [[Al Faisaly FC|Al-Faisaly]] and [[Al Taawoun FC|Al-Taawoun]], who joined as the promoted clubs from the [[Saudi First Division]]. No teams were relegated the previous season following the decision to increase the number of teams from 12 to 14.{{cite web |title=هل ستتغير خارطة دوري "زين"؟ |url=http://www.alriyadh.com/553669}} On 29 April, defending champions Al-Hilal won their 13th league title with two games to spare after a 1–0 home win over [[Al Raed FC|Al-Raed]].{{cite web |title= الهلال بطل دوري زين للمحترفين والاتفاق يرمي بالنصر الى المركز الخامس|url= http://www.slstat.com/spl2010-2011ar/news.php?id=382|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170929005740/http://www.slstat.com/spl2010-2011ar/news.php?id=382|url-status= dead|archive-date= 2017-09-29}} Al-Hilal ended the season without a single defeat – the first team ever to do so in a 26-game league season and the second team overall (the first was [[Al-Ettifaq FC|Al-Ettifaq]] in [[1982–83 Saudi Premier League|1983]], during an 18-game league season). [[Al-Hazem F.C.|Al-Hazem]] were the first team to be relegated following a 2–0 away defeat to [[Al Taawoun FC|Al-Taawoun]].{{cite web |title=التعاون يكتب نهاية الحزم في دوري زين والفتح يوقف مسيرة الفيصلي |url=http://www.slstat.com/spl2010-2011ar/news.php?id=362 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170929002626/http://www.slstat.com/spl2010-2011ar/news.php?id=362 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2017-09-29 }} [[Al Wehda FC|Al-Wehda]] became the second and final team to be relegated following the decision to dock 3 points from them.{{cite web |title=الانضباط تقرر حسم ثلاث نقاط والوحدة إلى الأولى والتعاون خارج كأس الأبطال |url=http://www.slstat.com/spl2010-2011ar/news.php?id=403 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170929003539/http://www.slstat.com/spl2010-2011ar/news.php?id=403 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2017-09-29 }} == Overview == === Changes === The SAFF announced that the number of teams in the league would be increased from 12 to 14. === Qualification and Prize money === The league champions, runners-up and third place as well as the winner of the [[2011 King Cup of Champions|King Cup of Champions]] qualified for the [[2012 AFC Champions League]]. The top six teams, and the [[2010–11 Saudi Crown Prince Cup|Crown Prince Cup]] winners and runners-up qualified for [[2012 King Cup of Champions|King Cup of Champions]]. Prize money: * First place: 2.5 million [[Saudi riyal|SAR]] * Second place: 1.5 million [[Saudi riyal|SAR]] * Third place: 1 million [[Saudi riyal|SAR]] ==Teams== 14 teams competed in the league – 12 teams from the previous season and two teams promoted from the [[2009–10 Saudi First Division League|First Division]]. No teams were relegated the previous season following the decision to increase the number of teams from 12 to 14.
